title: Evaluating TikTok Content on Gestational Diabetes Screening: Accuracy and Impact
screen_reason: Cross-sectional content analysis of TikTok posts about the oral glucose challenge test for gestational diabetes screening. The abstract reports one quantitative accuracy share with a recoverable denominator: 'Inaccurate or partially accurate posts made up 42% of educational posts' (educational posts n = 116). That is an item-level truth judgement, so CONTENT. JAMA/DISCERN scores are reported only as group comparisons, so they add no rows.

estimates.date: posts published 1 February 2020 - 31 October 2024; cross-sectional data collection on 1 December 2024
estimates.measure_type: % of educational TikTok posts about the oral glucose challenge test / gestational diabetes screening that were inaccurate or only partially accurate
estimates.value_raw: Inaccurate or partially accurate posts made up 42% of educational posts (educational posts n = 116)
estimates.denominator: 116 educational TikTok posts (of 306 posts meeting inclusion criteria out of 1,130 identified by the keywords glucola, glucose drink, gestational diabetes screening)
estimates.definition: Post's educational content classified as inaccurate or partially accurate (rather than accurate) with respect to gestational diabetes screening guidance; the numerator merges the 'inaccurate' and 'partially accurate' categories
estimates.misinfo_def: no formal definition in the abstract; accuracy was judged as accurate / partially accurate / inaccurate alongside 'JAMA, DISCERN criteria, and a harm-benefit analysis'
estimates.source_quote: Inaccurate or partially accurate posts made up 42% of educational posts and were most frequently shared by non-medical personnel.
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Study team coded each post for account type, theme, tone and readability and scored accuracy alongside JAMA and DISCERN criteria and a harm-benefit analysis; no coder count, adjudication rule or reliability statistic is reported in the abstract, and the external reference standard (screening guideline) is not named.
estimates.moderator_quote: A cross-sectional study was conducted on December 1, 2024, by first identifying posts in English on TikTok from February 1, 2020, to October 31, 2024, using keywords: glucola, glucose drink, and gestational diabetes screening. ... A total of 1,130 posts were identified, with 306 posts meeting inclusion criteria. Thematic analysis demonstrated that posts were for entertainment (n = 190) or educational (n = 116) purposes.
estimates.notes: breadth=misleading because the numerator merges 'inaccurate' with 'partially accurate', a broader-than-false category. The denominator is the EDUCATIONAL subset (116), not all 306 included posts - the abstract gives no accuracy share for the full sample, and 42% of 116 must not be rescaled to 306. denom_selection left blank: the corpus is a single-topic keyword search over a fixed window, neither rank-truncated nor multi-issue nor single-source (the restriction to educational posts is recorded in the denominator field instead). topic=health_other (pregnancy/gestational diabetes screening). Country is never stated; only 'posts in English'.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) JAMA and DISCERN scores are reported only as 'doctor-generated posts ... scored higher on JAMA and DISCERN criteria compared to other groups (p < 0.05)' - no share of posts above a threshold, so no QUALITY row (mean/rank comparison only). (2) Tone shares (80.7% neutral or positive about testing; 85.5% of doctors' posts positive; 67.6% of patient posts entertainment; 94.1% of doctors' content educational) are descriptive composition, not accuracy, so no rows. (3) Median view counts by harm-benefit class (44,600 vs 41,300 vs 6,449) are engagement, not exposure to misinformation with a denominator. (4) The 42% is not decomposable into 'inaccurate' vs 'partially accurate' from the abstract, so a stricter false-only row cannot be produced; a full-text check could split it. (5) Abstract-only record: the coding procedure, coder count and reliability could not be verified.

rob.design: Cross-sectional TikTok content analysis; keyword search (glucola, glucose drink, gestational diabetes screening) restricted to English posts published 1 Feb 2020 - 31 Oct 2024, collected 1 Dec 2024; 1,130 posts identified, 306 included (inclusion criteria not itemised in the abstract); posts scored with JAMA, DISCERN and a harm-benefit analysis plus an accuracy classification; number of coders, adjudication procedure and reliability statistics not reported in the abstract-only text.
rob.item6_quote: Posts were analyzed to determine account type, theme, tone, and readability ease, and then scored using JAMA, DISCERN criteria, and a harm-benefit analysis.
rob.item10_quote: A total of 1,130 posts were identified, with 306 posts meeting inclusion criteria. Thematic analysis demonstrated that posts were for entertainment (n = 190) or educational (n = 116) purposes. ... Inaccurate or partially accurate posts made up 42% of educational posts
